newsitem.title: UK: Killer flatworms besiege Scottish garden dwellers.
newsitem.headline: Killer flatworms besiege Scottish garden dwellers.

text.p: A voracious alien flatworm that sucks earthworms dry is laying siege to Scottish gardens, British scientists said on Thursday.
They said the previously unknown flatworm may have come from New Zealand and was threatening the local ecology.

Flatworms feed on earthworms by secreting digestive enzymes onto their victims and slurping up the soup that results. Earthworms are key to their ecological niches, aerating the soil and feeding birds, hedgehogs and other small mammals.

According to New Scientist magazine, two of the immigrant flatworms were found in a garden by Brian Gerard, a retired worm expert in Edinburgh. Checks with other experts confirmed that the species had never been seen before.
But Hugh Jones, a biologist at the University of Manchester, said he suspected it came from New Zealand.
"It seems to be as voracious for earthworms as New Zealand flatworms," he told New Scientist. "Should it become more widespread, it could become another threat to earthworms."

British earthworms are already under siege from flatworms harking from New Zealand and Australia. Accidentally introduced in the 1960s, they have been blamed for emptying gardens of the valued native creatures.
